references.text: The people of Israel were fed with manna in the wilderness – God feeds his people with bread miraculously, just as Jesus fed the five thousand.
Elisha fed a hundred men with twenty loaves of barley bread, and there was some left over, just as twelve baskets remained after Jesus' miracle.
The Lord promises to feed the poor of Zion with bread – a messianic promise fulfilled when Jesus feeds the crowd.
The Lord gives food to all in due time and feeds every living thing – Jesus' miracle of the loaves shows that he is the Lord who feeds his people.
The parallel passage in Matthew about the feeding of the five thousand, where everyone ate and was satisfied, and twelve baskets were left over.
At the feeding of the four thousand, everyone ate and was satisfied, and seven baskets were left over – a similar miracle.
The parallel passage in Mark where everyone ate and was satisfied, and they gathered twelve baskets of leftover pieces of bread.
In Mark's account of the feeding of the four thousand, they ate and were satisfied, and seven baskets were left over.
The parallel passage in John where Jesus tells the disciples to gather what is left over, and they fill twelve baskets with pieces of bread.
Jesus points back to the miracle of the loaves and urges the crowd to work for the food that lasts forever, not just the perishable kind.
